note: English LLM tells. Overlaps with slopster / deslop / vale-llm-slop by design — those are the reference implementations. Kept here so a bilingual README can be checked in one pass instead of wiring up Vale.

rules.name: em dash abuse
rules.msg: The single strongest English tell. Human technical writers rarely stack em dashes.
rules.fix: Use a period, a colon, or parentheses

rules.name: negation pivot (not X, but Y)
rules.msg: The contrastive pivot LLMs cannot stop producing.
rules.fix: State Y directly. Keep one only if you are correcting a real misconception

rules.name: definition opener
rules.msg: Opening with taxonomy instead of a picture. The reader wants to know what it fixes for them.
rules.fix: Lead with the reader's situation or the effect

rules.name: buzzwords
rules.msg: Marketing filler. Each one costs credibility in a technical README.

rules.name: inflated adjectives
rules.msg: Adjectives claiming quality the reader cannot verify.
rules.fix: Replace with the measurement or the output that proves it

rules.name: "it's worth noting"
rules.pattern: \b(?:it'?s worth noting|it is worth noting|it'?s important to note|notably,|importantly,)\b
rules.msg: Filler transition; deleting it loses nothing.

rules.name: "let's dive in"
rules.msg: Tutorial voice. README readers are here to copy a command.

rules.name: essay conclusion
rules.pattern: \b(?:in conclusion|to sum up|in summary,|all in all)\b
rules.msg: READMEs are not essays; nobody reads to the conclusion.

rules.name: "whether you're X or Y"
rules.msg: Audience-flattering template that names two audiences and serves neither.
rules.fix: Name the one real user and what they were doing when they needed this

rules.name: simply / just / easily
rules.msg: If it were simple the reader would not be reading this line.
rules.fix: Delete the adverb; if a step is genuinely one command, showing it proves that

rules.name: emoji in headings
rules.msg: The most visible marker of a generated README.
rules.fix: Drop it; use heading levels for structure

rules.name: hedging
rules.msg: Hedges leave the reader unable to decide whether to trust the line.
rules.fix: Give the condition under which it holds, or state it flatly
